edition.sessionCovered: Thu, Nov 5 (Democrats sweep Congress · oil crashes to $94 · gold breaks $4,100 · BTC reclaims $80K)
edition.stripNote: Thu 5 Nov. Democrats sweep both chambers. Oil crashes — Brent $94, WTI $87. Gold surges past $4,100. BTC reclaims $80K. Trump signals no further Iran strikes. NFP Fri.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Thu 5 Nov vs Wed 4 Nov close. Ranked best to worst.
edition.commodleHint: Democrats achieved a historic _____ winning both the House and Senate in the 2026 midterms

overview: Oil extended its post-midterm sell-off on Thursday, with Brent easing to approximately $94 per barrel — its lowest since late August — and WTI slipping below $88. The rout began Wednesday when Democrats swept both chambers of Congress, prompting Trump and Vance to blame the Iran war for Republican losses. Trump told the Financial Times that Washington had no immediate plans for further strikes and that a deal 'could happen.' Iran's Foreign Ministry said the country could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if its conditions were met. Brent has now fallen roughly 20% from last week's $117+ levels. The Energy Department announced a 300,000-barrel loan from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve. US crude inventories fell 900,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels last week, while distillate stocks dropped 3.6 million barrels — bullish supply data overwhelmed by the geopolitical shift. OPEC+ continues to hold December quotas unchanged, with the November 29 session set to determine 2027 targets.

Gold surged to approximately $4,125 per ounce — its highest since early October — as the dollar fell to a one-month low on the back of the Democratic sweep. Silver jumped above $52, platinum climbed toward $1,500 and palladium rebounded toward $1,000, reversing its 16-month low. Bitcoin consolidated above $80,000 after Wednesday's dramatic recovery from an election-night low of $75,618, driven by a $378-million short squeeze. Ethereum held near $2,440. The CME FedWatch probability of a December rate hike dropped to 78% from 87% at the start of the week. Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report (consensus 65K) is the next macro catalyst — a weak print could further ease rate-hike expectations and extend the cross-asset rotation into risk-on positions.

watchItems.title: Democrats sweep Congress — oil, gold and crypto react
watchItems.text: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the November 3 midterms, flipping at least six Republican Senate seats including Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa and Kansas. Trump and Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses. The political shift has immediate commodity implications: oil plunged 9% on Wednesday as traders priced in an end to the Iran conflict, gold surged above $4,100 as the dollar weakened to a one-month low, and Bitcoin recovered past $80,000 on a massive short squeeze. The new Democratic Congress is expected to resist fresh military authorisation for Iran and could pursue tariff rollbacks, easing trade tensions.

watchItems.title: Oil in freefall — Brent at two-month lows near $94
watchItems.text: Brent crude has fallen roughly 20% from last week's $117+ levels to approximately $94, its lowest since late August and the sharpest weekly decline since the Hormuz crisis began in February. Trump told the Financial Times the US has no immediate plans for further strikes, while Iran said it could reopen the strait within two days if its conditions are met. The Energy Department announced a 300,000-barrel loan from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve. Analysts warn the move is pricing in hope rather than a deal — a failed negotiation could quickly restore the risk premium toward $110+.

watchItems.title: Gold breaks $4,100 — dollar slides to one-month low
watchItems.text: Gold surged to approximately $4,125 per ounce, its highest since early October, as the dollar weakened sharply after the Democratic sweep. The CME FedWatch probability of a December rate hike dropped from 87% to 78%. Silver jumped above $52, platinum climbed toward $1,500 and palladium rebounded from 16-month lows. Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report (consensus 65K) is the next catalyst: a weak print could further ease rate-hike expectations and extend the precious metals rally. Support for gold sits at $3,980–$4,000; resistance at $4,115.

watchItems.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80K — short squeeze defies ETF outflows
watchItems.text: Bitcoin staged a dramatic recovery from an election-night low of $75,618 to above $80,000, driven by a massive short squeeze that liquidated $378 million in short positions in a single hour. US spot Bitcoin ETFs had seen $1.16 billion in net outflows over three sessions before the election. The Democratic sweep could reshape the crypto-regulatory landscape — the new Congress may pursue a more structured framework for digital assets. BTC remains about 36% below its all-time high of $126,080. The Fear and Greed Index rose from 26 to 34 but remains in fear territory.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: Rebounding from $3,876 Oct low · broke $4,100 on dollar weakness
desk.sum: Gold surged above $4,100 on Thursday, reaching approximately $4,125 — its highest since early October — as the dollar slid to a one-month low following the Democratic sweep of Congress. The weaker dollar and falling oil prices, which ease the case for aggressive rate hikes, combined to create a powerful tailwind. The CME FedWatch probability of a December rate hike has dropped to 78% from 87% at the start of the week. Support at $3,980–$4,000; resistance at $4,115. Friday's nonfarm payrolls report (consensus 65K) is the next catalyst.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: Rebounding from $49.85 · dollar weakness lifts
desk.sum: Silver extended its post-midterm rally to approximately $52.50, gaining roughly 5% from its pre-election level of $49.85. The metal benefited from dollar weakness and the broader precious metals bid. The gold-silver ratio held near 78.6 as both metals rallied on the back of the Democratic sweep. A further dovish shift in Fed expectations, particularly if Friday's NFP disappoints, would provide additional support.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $87 · Brent down ~20% from last week's $117+ · Iran peace hopes accelerate
desk.sum: Brent slipped to approximately $94 on Thursday, extending its post-midterm sell-off to a two-month low. The barrel is now down roughly 20% from last week's $117+ levels as traders aggressively price in an end to the Iran conflict. Trump told the Financial Times the US had no immediate plans for further strikes, while Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if its conditions were met. WTI fell below $88. The Energy Department announced a 300,000-barrel loan from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve. US crude inventories fell 900,000 barrels to 409.8M bbl, and distillate stocks dropped 3.6M bbl — bullish supply data overwhelmed by the geopolitical shift.

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME $14,015/t · Shanghai spot premiums at yearly high
desk.sum: Copper held near $6.35 per pound on Thursday as macro uncertainty continued to weigh. LME copper closed at $14,015 per tonne, down 0.14%, with long liquidation reducing open interest. Shanghai spot premiums surged to a yearly high of 1,900 yuan per tonne amid tightening inventory — SMM estimates stocks across major Chinese regions fell to approximately 80,000 tonnes, down 24,900 tonnes week-on-week. The weaker dollar provides support but the Democratic sweep raises tariff-rollback expectations.

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Under heavy pressure from Hormuz peace hopes · YTD +30%
desk.sum: Newcastle coal dropped to approximately $141 per tonne as the Hormuz peace narrative intensified. If negotiations succeed and Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity return to market, coal-switching economics would weaken significantly in Asia and Europe. Year-to-date gains have compressed from 40% to roughly 30%. The March precedent — when coal fell below $130 on earlier Iran peace talks — suggests further downside if a deal materialises.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Rebounding from $1,437 low · +4% in two sessions
desk.sum: Platinum rallied to approximately $1,498 on Thursday, rebounding sharply from its recent low near $1,437 as the dollar weakened and precious metals benefited from the post-midterm bid. The metal gained roughly 4% over two sessions since the election results. PPLT (platinum ETF) surged 5.6% on Wednesday. The supply deficit narrative (WPIC) and reduced rate-hike expectations provide near-term support, though the medium-term outlook remains clouded by surplus projections.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Rebounding from $940 · 16-month low · +6% over two sessions
desk.sum: Palladium bounced to approximately $998 on Thursday, recovering from its 16-month low of $940 as the Democratic sweep lifted risk sentiment across precious metals. The metal gained approximately 6% over two sessions, the strongest performer on the desk. However, structural headwinds persist: EV adoption and the shift toward platinum in catalytic converters continue to erode long-term demand. Nornickel's plant overhaul provides some supply-side support.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~10 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · Trump signals no further strikes · Iran offers 2-day reopening
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz situation shifted markedly after the Democratic sweep of Congress. Trump told the Financial Times that Washington had no immediate plans for further strikes and that a deal 'could happen.' Iran's Foreign Ministry said it could reopen the strait within two days if the US meets its conditions — including lifting the naval blockade and returning frozen assets. Qatar and Pakistan continue mediating. The new Democratic Congress is expected to resist fresh military authorisation, increasing diplomatic pressure to resolve the standoff. Approximately 10 transits per day versus 85 pre-war.

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: −9% m/m · weaker dollar supports
desk.sum: December corn firmed to approximately 446¢ per bushel, supported by the weaker dollar which improves US export competitiveness. Harvest pressure is moderating as the US crop nears completion. The post-midterm trade outlook is more favourable, with Democrats likely to pursue tariff rollbacks. Managed money remains short but the dollar's slide to a one-month low may prompt some short covering.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: −15% m/m · dollar weakness supports
desk.sum: December wheat edged up to approximately 600¢ per bushel, reclaiming the $6 level on the back of dollar weakness. The dollar's slide to a one-month low after the midterm results improved the competitiveness of US wheat exports. However, ample global supply and resumed Russian grain shipments from Azov ports continue to cap rallies. Record managed-money short positions and adequate world stocks limit upside.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: −5% m/m · Dem win may ease US-China tensions
desk.sum: Soybeans edged up to approximately 1,196¢ per bushel, buoyed by the weaker dollar. The Democratic victory may ease US-China trade tensions and improve soybean export prospects over the medium term. However, competitive Brazilian production and the approaching South American harvest continue to weigh on the near-term outlook. Chinese buying interest remains muted.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $2,440 · recovered from $75,618 election-night low · $378M short squeeze
desk.sum: Bitcoin consolidated above $80,000 on Thursday, holding near $80,500 after Wednesday's dramatic recovery from an election-night low of $75,618. The move was triggered by a massive short squeeze — $378 million in shorts were liquidated in a single hour on Wednesday, representing 81% of that hour's forced closures across crypto. Democrats winning both chambers could shift the crypto-regulatory landscape. Ethereum held near $2,440. BTC remains about 36% below its all-time high of $126,080. The Fear and Greed Index rose from 26 to 34 but remains in fear territory.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM ~$32 · TTF ~$31/MBtu · HH $2.99 · Hormuz deal could compress to mid-$20s
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) held near $31.76 per MMBtu, largely unchanged. The Hormuz peace narrative looms large: if the strait reopens, Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity would flow back to Asian and European buyers, potentially compressing JKM toward the mid-$20s. The Democratic sweep of Congress increases the probability of a diplomatic resolution. Henry Hub firmed slightly to $2.99. European TTF holds near $31/MBtu.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait $765 · Dem Congress raises peace odds · at risk from Hormuz deal
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,200 per tonne. The Democratic sweep of Congress increases the probability of a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, which would release Middle East sulfur flows and rapidly ease the acute supply squeeze in fertiliser and mining supply chains. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Chinese domestic sulfur is approximately 7,200 yuan per tonne.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · Dem Congress may ease trade policy
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367 per tonne. BPC settled a new India contract at $383 per tonne CFR, approximately $35 above China's 2026 benchmark. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. The Democratic sweep may ease trade tensions, potentially facilitating broader fertiliser market flows.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: Off 105k high · consolidating at lows since mid-Oct
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) continues to consolidate near 90,000 yuan per tonne after declining sharply from the 105,000-yuan October 9 high. SMM expects low-level sideways consolidation with supply still contracting under Document No. 46 export controls but demand remaining weak. The Democratic takeover of Congress could shift the dynamic on US-China strategic mineral relations.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: Up >130% since early 2025 · China Ga ~¥1,740/kg · Dem Congress may shift China policy
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, up over 130% since early 2025. China's Document No. 46 export controls retain a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium. The new Democratic Congress may pursue a different approach to US-China strategic mineral relations, though near-term supply dynamics are unchanged.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Down from $5.44 in 2024 · steel demand soft
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds near $5.02 per pound, soft as steel demand weakens. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but the timing of large-scale adoption remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Hovering near $5,400 · ICE inventories at 2.5-yr high · Q3 grindings +14.3%
desk.sum: ICE cocoa held near $5,427 per tonne, little changed. Rising ICE warehouse inventories — at a 2.5-year high of 3.69 million bags as of late October — continue to cap rallies. However, Q3 cocoa grindings rose 14.3%, beating expectations, with Asia up 29.2% and Europe up 3.2%. StoneX projects 2026/27 global output to fall 9.6% to 4.74 million tonnes, which could turn the current surplus into a deficit.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: DRC quotas 96,600 t/yr · flat on week · −14% m/m
desk.sum: Cobalt holds at approximately $33,525 per tonne, flat on the week and down about 14% on the month. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes per year through 2027 to support prices, but the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce demand. Glencore expects DRC exports to normalise in line with quotas.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Futures ~¥91k · down from ¥97.5k · halved from May ¥200k+
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot fell to ¥92,850 per tonne, down 1% and continuing its decline from ¥97,500 earlier in the week. The selloff extends from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000, driven by the SMM inventory restatement, Australian mine restarts at Bald Hill and Finniss, and expectations of a growing surplus. Lithium futures on the Guangzhou exchange traded around ¥91,000. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), little changed. Southeast Asian supply remains tight with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Auto-sector demand remains solid, supported by replacement-tyre cycles.
